content.text: : fungicidal agent which inhibits squalene epoxidase, an essential enzyme in fungal sterol synthesis; produces a deficiency of ergosterol and an accumulation of squalene inside the fungal cell resulting in cell death
: treatment of onychomycosis of the toenail or fingernail due to dermatophytes; demonstrated superiority in efficacy over griseofulvin
: HA, increased LFTs, skin rashes, GI upset, abdominal pain, taste disturbances, dyspepsia
: hepatotoxicity, permanent taste disturbances, depression, neutropenia, TTP, HUS, SJS/TEN, DRESS, erythema multiforme
: continuous regimen for toenails, pulse-dosing regimen for fingernails – 2
line for pts who failed terbinafine
: recommended regimen for toenails is 150mg once weekly for 12wks – 2
: inhibits the fungal enzyme leucyl-tRNA synthetase that is required for protein synthesis; termination of cell growth and cell death

roles.drugs: Oral terbinafine (highest effectiveness; eg, 250 mg daily, 6 weeks fingernails); main CI chronic or active liver disease
